cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: Obesity: BMI over 30. Affects 28% of UK adults and rising in children. Caused by sustained positive energy balance (calories in exceed calories out). Increases risk of type 2 diabetes, heart disease, stroke, and certain cancers.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: Type 2 diabetes: the body becomes resistant to insulin or doesn't produce enough. Strongly linked to obesity, physical inactivity, and diets high in sugar and refined carbohydrates. Management includes weight loss, exercise, and reduced sugar intake.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: Cardiovascular disease (CVD): includes heart disease and stroke. Risk factors include high blood pressure, high LDL cholesterol, smoking, obesity, and physical inactivity. Diet influences: excess saturated fat raises LDL cholesterol; excess salt raises blood pressure; fruit and vegetables provide antioxidants.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: Tooth decay (dental caries): caused by bacteria fermenting sugars to produce acid that erodes tooth enamel. Frequency of sugar consumption matters more than total amount. Prevention: reduce sugar frequency, brush twice daily with fluoride toothpaste, visit the dentist.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: Iron-deficiency anaemia: most common nutritional deficiency globally. Particularly affects women (menstrual losses), teenagers (rapid growth), and vegetarians (non-haem iron is poorly absorbed). Symptoms: fatigue, pallor, breathlessness, poor concentration.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: Osteoporosis: weakened bones prone to fracture. Linked to inadequate calcium and vitamin D intake, particularly in post-menopausal women. Prevention: adequate calcium, vitamin D, and weight-bearing exercise throughout life.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: Bowel cancer: linked to low fibre intake, high red and processed meat consumption, obesity, and alcohol. The UK has one of the highest rates in Europe. Increasing fibre to 30g/day and reducing processed meat are key dietary strategies.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: Food poverty: inability to afford or access nutritious food. Affects diet quality — cheaper foods are often energy-dense but nutrient-poor, contributing to both obesity and micronutrient deficiencies in deprived communities.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: The Sugar Reduction Programme: PHE challenged the food industry to reduce sugar in key product categories by 20% by 2020. The Soft Drinks Industry Levy ('sugar tax') reduced sugar in drinks by approximately 29%.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: The National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS) monitors UK dietary habits and nutritional status, providing data for public health policy.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: Socioeconomic factors: diet quality is strongly linked to income and education. Healthier diets cost more per calorie than unhealthy ones, creating inequality in health outcomes.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Diet-Related Health Issues
cards.back: Prevention strategies: education, food labelling (traffic light system), reformulation, taxation, advertising restrictions, and improving access to healthy foods in deprived areas.

cards.back: 1. For Diet-Related Health Issues questions, show every step of your working clearly — method marks count even if the final answer is wrong 2.
